title: Reproducible resting-state HRV on MIT-BIH

dataset.name: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database
dataset.citation: Moody GB, Mark RG. The impact of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. IEEE Eng Med Biol Mag. 2001;20(3):45-50.

proposition: On the gold-standard MIT-BIH ECG (real record 100), the ecosystem reproduces standard resting-state HRV: R-peak detection is exact (F1 = 1.000), time-domain metrics match the Task-Force definitions to < 1e-6 and agree with the RHRV reference within its known first-interval drop (< 0.5%), and the resting-HR op-DAG replays byte-identically from a frozen pre-registration.

claims.statement: mean heart rate (record 100 resting run, MLII), bpm
mean RR interval (record 100 resting run, MLII), ms

cross_tool.data: REAL — MIT-BIH record 100, first 5 min, N = 370 RR (annotation-derived)
cross_tool.note: PhysioECG matches the Task-Force 1996 standard definitions to < 1e-6 (column value == standard_def); agreement with RHRV is within RHRV's first-interval drop.

open_questions.q: pNN50 is sensitive to the >50 vs >=50 ms threshold and to whether RR is exact-integer or reconstructed as floating point from cumulative beat times; on a deterministic synthetic series these choices span 0% / 22.2% / 50.5% (artifacts/pnn50_diagnosis.csv). This is a documented numeric-reconstruction artefact, not a defect: on the REAL MIT-BIH RR series no diff lands on the 50 ms boundary and PhysioECG (6.78%) and RHRV (6.49%) agree. The pipeline therefore adopts the Task-Force >50 / exact-integer definition. RESOLVED — not escalated.
